title: P42: variance-matched orthogonal hidden-matrix initialization
description: P42: reinitialize all 16 hidden projection matrices orthogonally with gain 0.02 * sqrt(max(rows, columns)), preserving the incumbent expected element second moment. Better initial signal propagation may improve the policy handed to fixed downstream expert iteration under the existing Muon pretraining setup.
hypothesis: Incumbent 040 scores 294/265/250 (exact mean 269.666667). Muon improved transfer in 030 and subsequent optimizer experiments produced 040, while depth-scaled residual initialization (020, on the older AdamW baseline) and recent z-loss (042) failed. No prior record tests orthogonal initialization. Initially equal singular values on the supported subspace may avoid poorly conditioned hidden transformations and help the short Muon trajectory learn reusable proof features. This is an unverified mechanism: rectangular projections cannot be isometries in both directions, and useful anisotropy may instead be suppressed. QKV is initialized as one 768-by-256 matrix, not as three independent orthogonal matrices; the existing optimizer still splits Q/K/V updates. Extra initialization draws change the global RNG state but the seed policy and separately seeded data generator remain unchanged. Only the downstream three-seed mean decides keep/discard.
expected_delta: Conditional on improvement, +5 to +20 dev-transfer solves at length >=7 versus exact baseline mean 269.666667; plausible downside -20 to -60. Expect one-time QR initialization cost below 5 seconds and no inference latency change; construction time is charged to the fixed 300-second pretraining budget.

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon hidden matrices throughout; continuous AdamW auxiliary

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: sqrt(max(1, rows/columns)) per orthogonalized matrix: Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 2, fc2 1
muon.schedule: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW; muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: All 16 hidden projection parameters remain in Muon. Four qkv.weight matrices of shape (768,256) use independent Q/K/V updates, represented as a batch of three (256,256) matrices; proj/fc1/fc2 remain unchanged.
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: After elementwise Nesterov momentum, reshape each QKV update to (3,256,256); independently Frobenius-normalize and run five batched Newton-Schulz steps; reshape back before applying. No extra learning-rate multiplier. Momentum and weight decay stay elementwise and unchanged.

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, head.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters throughout; hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW
optimizer.decay_convention: Muon lr*0.01 equals auxiliary AdamW lr*0.1, preserving incumbent per-update shrinkage at every schedule fraction, including the former finish window; integrated decay can differ with throughput.
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 before both optimizers
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights only; pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW

config.init: Fork default construction, then orthogonal_ on every 2D block parameter after moving to device. Gain = 0.02 * sqrt(max(rows, columns)); exact element second moment 0.0004. All 16 hidden matrices: qkv (768,256), proj (256,256), fc1 (1024,256), fc2 (256,1024) in each of four blocks. QKV initialized jointly. Embedding, readout, biases and LayerNorm retain their original draws/values. No reinitialization during RL.
